sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for scan tests
sections.what: Loads the test runner, the scan model, slide builders, schedule helpers, calculation helpers and types.
sections.why: Gives the tests every function they check.
sections.watch_out: Imports reach into library folders, so moving files breaks them.

sections.name: project
sections.title: Shared fake project
sections.what: Defines a fake dairy project with a twenty percent cost overrun and zero delay.
sections.why: Gives every test one common starting record.
sections.watch_out: Changing this record changes several tests at once.

sections.name: input (part 1)
sections.title: Scan tests part one
sections.what: Defines a fake scan input, then runs tests for cost and month calculations, schedule percentages, appendix contents, chart percentage labels, final presentation values and legacy runs. Starts a slide geometry test, whose body was not supplied.
sections.why: Covers the main calculations and the slides that show them.
sections.watch_out: The final values test expects the input snapshot to stay unchanged, so any code that edits it fails here.

sections.name: input (part 2)
sections.title: Checks for scan slide building
sections.what: Runs the slide builder on made-up projects and confirms the result is sound. Every element has a unique ID and valid position numbers, every project name appears on a slide, and a large set of projects still produces every chart point and exactly one summary slide. It also checks that the cover image follows each project's industry.
sections.why: Likely reason: to catch broken or missing slides, lost project points, and wrong cover images before a deck reaches a user. The sample objects `input` and `project` are defined earlier in the file, which is not visible here.
sections.watch_out: The cover image checks use exact file names such as industry-nuclear.jpg, so renaming image files will break these tests.

summary: A set of node tests for the scan pipeline covering calculations, schedule percentages, appendix contents, chart labels and final presentation values. The last test section was not supplied.
purpose: Makes sure scan results and slides show correct numbers.
why: Likely reason: several parts feed one presentation, so tests catch drift between them.
how: Defines a fake dairy project. Tests cost deviation and month calculations with zero values, schedule overrun percentages with missing or zero baselines, appendix inclusion rules, percentage labels on the chart, final values that do not change their inputs, and legacy runs that are not filled from live data. Starts a slide geometry test whose body was not supplied.
inputs: Fixture projects and inputs defined in the file, and the scan calculation and slide modules.
outputs: Pass and fail results from the node test runner.
risks: Fixtures are fake and may not match real data. The geometry test is not described here.
debug: Use the failing test name to find the matching module, then compare its output with the expected value.
